clinician.final_diagnosis: A tension pneumothorax, possibly secondary to underlying COVID-19
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 36-year-old man with 3 weeks of respiratory symptoms (dry cough, fevers) presented via ambulance with acute deterioration over 4 hours featuring left-sided pleuritic chest pain, severe respiratory distress (RR 50, SpO2 88-90% on 15 L/min oxygen), and hemodynamic compromise (tachycardia 150 bpm, elevated JVP 3 cm, borderline hypotension 110/65 mmHg). Physical examination revealed absent breath sounds, reduced vocal fremitus, and asymmetrical chest expansion on the left. Portable chest radiograph confirmed a large left-sided pneumothorax with mediastinal shift and radiological signs of tension (E001). Immediate emergency needle decompression was performed with a 14-gauge cannula in the second intercostal space mid-clavicular line (E007), followed by insertion of a 12-French Seldinger chest drain into the left axilla (E008). The patient demonstrated immediate clinical and physiological improvement within one hour, with oxygen requirements decreasing from 15 L/min to 4 L/min and normalization of respiratory and heart rates, accompanied by radiological evidence of lung re-expansion (E009). Initial COVID-19 PCR testing was negative; however, following review by the infectious diseases team, the clinical and epidemiological context led to assessment that he likely had COVID-19 with a false-negative result due to delayed presentation (E010).

Assessment by infectious diseases team that patient likely had COVID-19 despite negative initial PCR due to delayed presentation
